text:
ivy: Heads-up — found a flaky resume case in the sample-app streaming demo. After abort+reconnect the browser client sometimes receives a few nonprintable bytes then pieces of two SSE events glued together and the JSON parse fails.
omar: which runtime? SDK version? can you paste raw bytes?
ivy: Browser JS SDK (fetch polyfilled) on mac; behind our dev mitm proxy. Raw capture excerpt:```[recv] 0x00 0x0b 0x7b 0x22 0x74 0x65 0x78 0x74  -> leading NUL + LF then '{"text'\n[recv] data: {"id":"10","seq":2,"text":"later"}\n[recv] data: {"id":"9","seq":1,"text":"first"}\n[parser] combined => '\\u0000\\n{\"id\":\"10\",\"seq\":2,\"text\":\"later\"}{\"id\":\"9\",\"seq\":1,\"text\":\"first\"}' -> JSON parse error```
qa_lee: only hits via dev proxy? repro w/ curl or direct host?
ivy: Direct to backend clean. `curl --no-buffer` no repro. Only flakey behind dev proxy when the connection pool is warm and we had a recent abort. ~3-6% reconnects fail.
omar: could be the proxy interleaving writes when a tiny auth POST or health check reuses the same backend connection. Did you see auth refresh around the same time?
ivy: yes sometimes an auth refresh POST to /oauth/refresh overlaps the reconnect. I added repro steps to sample-app/streaming/REPRO.md: set token TTL to 1s and trigger reconnect during refresh.
qa_lee: thanks. What's the short-term mitigation for SDK users?
omar: propose defensive client changes: 1) ignore leading control bytes <= 0x1f before first printable char for a resumed stream (log metric when this happens), 2) treat incoming bytes as a stream and only split SSE events on full delimiter `\n\n` (don't assume network chunk = event), 3) optional small reorder buffer keyed by `seq` (or `id`) that holds up to N=8 events or 200ms and reorders if needed.
ivy: I wired a quick local patch (feature-flagged) that trims leading control bytes and buffers until `\n\n`; that fixed my local flakiness. Will open an SDK PR with unit tests.
qa_lee: please add tests: leading-control trimming, interleaved-write harness (server that purposely writes seq2 then seq1), and ensure `retry:` and comment lines aren't dropped.
omar: infra: can you capture a pcap/tcpdump next time? If pooled writes are the cause we should be able to see interleaved TCP segments. Also try toggling keepalive/pooling for the dev proxy to reproduce.
infra-bot: INF-1602 created: "dev-proxy: investigate pooled connections causing interleaved chunk writes / leading control bytes on SSE resume". Requesting pcap and keepalive-off experiment on test host.
devex-bot: DEX-1603 opened: "streaming: resume defensive parser (trim nonprintables, buffer-on-delimiter, optional reorder buffer) + infra pcap triage". Link added to sample-app repro.
omar: sample repro server snippet (added to REPRO.md):```js
// simulate interleave: write part for seq=2 then seq=1
res.write('\x00data: {"id":"10","seq":2,"text":"later"}\n\n');
setTimeout(()=>res.write('data: {"id":"9","seq":1,"text":"first"}\n\n'), 1);
```
ivy: I'll attach logs and the pcap once infra provides it. Plan: ship SDK parser change behind a flag, collect telemetry counters `sse.trim_bytes` and `sse.reorder_events` for a week, and keep INF-1602 open until infra confirms root cause.
qa_lee: Agreed. Do not silently enable reorder buffer in prod without telemetry.
omar: +1. small thread but actionable. :thumbsup:
